title: Tactical Fanout Failover Governor: latency-aware fanout, geo-pinning, and capacity gating
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Introduce a lightweight request 'governor' that orchestrates short-circuit fanout decisions for multi-region requests. The governor enforces latency SLOs by combining: (1) fast-path latency-based routing, (2) sticky geo-pinning heuristics for TTL-bound affinity, and (3) capacity-aware gating with circuit-breaker and token-based shedder. This ticket drives the design, prototype, and an incremental rollout for the new steering component.
background: We continue to see tail-latency spikes when cross-region fanouts increase under bursty load. Current steering policies either over-prioritize locality (causing cold-region overloads) or aggressively hedged fanouts (increasing cost and backend pressure). We need a middle ground that preserves caller SLOs while protecting scarce Dedicated capacity and reducing noisy cascading failovers.
goals: 1) Reduce 99th-percentile end-to-end latency violations by 25% for multi-region requests. 2) Prevent capacity blowouts in warmed-up Dedicated pools during cross-region incidents. 3) Provide an operator-visible mode for gradual rollout and canarying.
non_goals: Replacing global routing fabric or rewriting autoscaler logic. This is not a global placement algorithm; it is a request-time governor to guide existing routers and admission controllers.
proposed_design: - Fast-path: measure per-region p50 and p95 from last 30s; prefer region if p95 < latency_slo * 0.85 and availability healthy. - Affinity: maintain short TTL geo-pins (default 60s) for clients that show stable low-latency; add jitter decay after failures. - Capacity gate: integrate with pool credits; if pool credit < low_watermark, flip to soft-pin or failover pool. - Circuit breaker: per-pool CB opens on a composite signal (error-rate, latency breach, credit depletion) with exponential backoff and probe windows. - Shedder: token-bucket shedder that prefers soft-degradation (lower tokenization cost path or smaller batch sizes) before hard rejects. - Instrumentation: emit decision traces for each request (decision_reason, candidate_regions, chosen_region, fallback_path, tokens_used).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated behind rollout:governor. 2) Canary to 1% of traffic in region-us-west-2 (2 days). 3) Expand to 10% after stability checks (7 days). 4) Enable capacity gate + shedder in canary after 10% (another 7 days). 5) Gradual global rollout with traffic ramp if no P0 incidents. 6) Quick rollback path: disable flag or switch to legacy router policy.
metrics_and_slos: Primary SLO: request end-to-end p95 < 220ms for textgen small payloads. Metrics to track: region_selection_latency, decision_time_microsec, chosen_region_p95, pool_credit_remaining, shed_rate, cb_open_rate, downstream_5xx_rate, cost_per_request. Alerts: p95 > threshold OR shed_rate > 1% OR cb_open_rate > 0.5% for 5m.
test_plan: Unit tests for governor decision logic with synthetic region profiles. Integration: staged canary traffic using traffic-replay harness. Chaos tests: simulated region latency spikes, simulated Dedicated pool credit exhaustion, and concurrent failover with autoscaler. Load tests: verify shedder behavior under 10k rps across 3 regions.
open_questions: What is the canonical window for rolling p95 calculations (30s vs 60s)?
Should geo-pin TTL be configurable per-client or per-customer?
How aggressive should token-bucket thresholds be for soft vs hard shedding?
Can we reuse existing pool credit metrics or add a lightweight shepherd metric for quick decisions?
decisions: Use 30s sliding window for p95 as default (can be tuned by release toggles)
Default geo-pin TTL set to 60s with exponential backoff on failures
Circuit-breaker composite signal includes latency+errors+credit depletion
Emit a single decision trace span per request to avoid trace-cardinality explosion
implementation_notes: Prototype as a stateless sidecar module callable by the request director; keep state in fast in-memory LRU for recent client pins
Leverage existing pool_credit metric (instrumented in runtime) and expose a fast GRPC endpoint for governor polling
Add feature-flag and per-customer opt-out for Dedicated customers who want guaranteed pinning
Avoid per-request heavy-weight telemetry; aggregate decisions with sampling (1%) and full traces on anomalies
